newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia to issue bonds to cover state debt to NBY.
newsitem.headline: Serbia to issue bonds to cover state debt to NBY.

text.p: Serbia plans to issue bonds to cover its debt to the central bank incurred from early 1994, Tanjug news agency reported on Friday.

The government wants to clear its 350 million dinar ($68.7 million) debt by issuing one-year bonds, with a face value of 500,000 and five million dinars. The issue date of bonds is December 31, 1996, Tanjug said.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) extended the 350 million dinar credit to the Republic of Serbia for covering public deficit on January 24, 1994.
In 1994, the dinar was pegged at par to the German mark.
"Serbia will clear its entire debt to the NBY through this operation," Garib Hadzini, Serbian Deputy Finance Minister told Reuters.

Hadzini said the interest rate on bonds will be equal to the official NBY discount rate. The discount rate is set every month and has been kept unchanged since June 1996 at a monthly 4.5 percent or 68.15 percent a year.
"Interest will be paid to investors quarterly, eight days after the three-month period expires. The principle will be reimbursed on December 31, 1997," Hadzini said.
In the first stage of what Hadzini called a monetary neutral operation, bonds will be bought by the central bank.
Thereafter, NBY can place bonds on the market and sell them to domestic or foreign investors, companies and individuals, Hadzini said.
There was no one at the central bank immediately available for comment.
Serbian state bonds will be the first state debt paper issued since 1994 when the economic stabilisation programme was launched.
One-year bonds will become the longest term investment on the Yugoslav fledgling financial market. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
